description: DeviceRequestAllocationResult contains the allocation result for one request.

adminAccess.description:
adminAccess indicates that this device was allocated for administrative access. See the corresponding request field for a definition of mode.

Admin access is disabled if this field is unset or set to false, otherwise it is enabled.

bindingConditions.description: bindingConditions contains a copy of the BindingConditions from the corresponding ResourceSlice at the time of allocation.

bindingFailureConditions.description: bindingFailureConditions contains a copy of the BindingFailureConditions from the corresponding ResourceSlice at the time of allocation.

consumedCapacity.description:
consumedCapacity tracks the amount of capacity consumed per device as part of the claim request. The consumed amount may differ from the requested amount: it is rounded up to the nearest valid value based on the device’s requestPolicy if applicable (i.e., may not be less than the requested amount).

The total consumed capacity for each device must not exceed the DeviceCapacity's Value.

This field is populated only for devices that allow multiple allocations. All capacity entries are included, even if the consumed amount is zero. The domain prefix in the capacity name may be omitted if it is the same as the driver name.

ConsumedCapacity may have at most 32 entries. The values must not be negative.

consumedCounters.description:
consumedCounters records resolved valueFrom consumption for the single device identified by this allocation result, grouped by counter set in that device's pool. Each result records only its own request-dependent amounts. The scheduler sums these amounts across non-admin allocation results, including multiple shares of the same device. Releasing one allocation releases its recorded amounts without changing those of other allocations.

Quantities are resolved at allocation time from the matching claim capacity requests, including consumptionPolicy rounding. They may therefore be greater than the requested amounts. If the claim omits a mapped capacity request, consumption uses the shared counter's policy default, or its full value when no default is defined. All resolved valueFrom counters are included, even when their quantity is zero.

The recorded amounts and counter set references remain authoritative if ResourceSlice mappings, defaults, or policies change. A mapping change does not move an existing allocation's consumption to a different counter set. DRA drivers can use these amounts without access to ResourceSlices.

Fixed counter consumption is not recorded here. The scheduler determines fixed consumption from current ResourceSlices, including consumptionPolicy rounding, and counts it once per (driver, pool, device) with at least one non-admin allocation. If the device definition is missing, its fixed consumption is not counted. Current fixed consumption is added to the recorded request-dependent consumption; changing a counter from valueFrom to value does not replace the recorded amounts.

Current counter values still define the total budget. Reducing a counter below its recorded consumption prevents further counter consumption; existing allocation results are not changed. Recorded amounts are still counted if the allocated device is no longer present in current ResourceSlices. Amounts that refer to a missing counter set or counter are ignored.

ResourceSlice updates do not resize or revoke existing allocations. Drivers must ensure that updates remain compatible with existing allocations, or arrange for affected allocations to be released first.

This field is populated only for non-admin allocations when DRASharedConsumableCapacity is enabled. An absent field means that no request-dependent consumption was recorded, including for allocations made before the feature was enabled. If this field is absent, the scheduler counts this allocation's request-dependent counter consumption as zero. It does not reconstruct that consumption from the device's current valueFrom mappings.

The list contains at most 2 counter sets (the maximum a device may consume in a ResourceSlice), keyed by counter set name. Its order has no correspondence to the order of counter sets or devices in ResourceSlices.

items.description:
CounterSetConsumption records one allocation's resolved valueFrom consumption from one counter set. The containing DeviceRequestAllocationResult identifies the allocated device and its pool.

For example, two allocations sharing a device may consume 2Gi and 3Gi from a "memory" counter. Each result records only its own amount; together they consume 5Gi. Releasing the first allocation leaves 3Gi charged. If the device also consumes one fixed "slots" counter, that charge is accounted for separately from current ResourceSlices. With unchanged slice definitions, the fixed charge remains until the last non-admin allocation is released.

counterSet.description: counterSet identifies a counter set in the pool named by the containing allocation result.

counters.description: counters records this allocation's resolved quantity for each counter in the set. The map contains at most 32 counters; each quantity must be non-negative.

device.description: device references one device instance via its name in the driver's resource pool. It must be a DNS label.

driver.description:
driver specifies the name of the DRA driver whose kubelet plugin should be invoked to process the allocation once the claim is needed on a node.

Must be a DNS subdomain and should end with a DNS domain owned by the vendor of the driver. It should use only lower case characters.

pool.description:
pool specifies the name together with the driver name and the device name field identify which device was allocated (`<driver name>/<pool name>/<device name>`).

Must not be longer than 253 characters and may contain one or more DNS sub-domains separated by slashes.

request.description:
request is the name of the request in the claim which caused this device to be allocated. If it references a subrequest in the firstAvailable list on a DeviceRequest, this field must include both the name of the main request and the subrequest using the format <main request>/<subrequest>.

Multiple devices may have been allocated per request.

shareID.description: shareID uniquely identifies an individual allocation share of the device, used when the device supports multiple simultaneous allocations. It serves as an additional map key to differentiate concurrent shares of the same device.

skipNodeOperations.description: skipNodeOperations lists node-local resource operations (gRPC calls) that will be skipped for this allocated device when determining whether operations are necessary on the node. If all allocated devices for a driver in a claim skip an operation, that gRPC call will be skipped. It is a copy of the ResourceSlice.spec.skipNodeOperations value at the time when the device was allocated.

tolerations.description:
tolerations is a copy of all tolerations specified in the request at the time when the device got allocated.

The maximum number of tolerations is 16.

This is a beta field and requires enabling the DRADeviceTaints feature gate.

items.description: The ResourceClaim this DeviceToleration is attached to tolerates any taint that matches the triple <key,value,effect> using the matching operator <operator>.

effect.description: effect indicates the taint effect to match. Empty means match all taint effects. When specified, allowed values are NoSchedule and NoExecute.

key.description: key is the taint key that the toleration applies to. Empty means match all taint keys. If the key is empty, operator must be Exists; this combination means to match all values and all keys. Must be a label name.

operator.description: operator represents a key's relationship to the value. Valid operators are Exists and Equal. Defaults to Equal. Exists is equivalent to wildcard for value, so that a ResourceClaim can tolerate all taints of a particular category.

tolerationSeconds.description: tolerationSeconds represents the period of time the toleration (which must be of effect NoExecute, otherwise this field is ignored) tolerates the taint. By default, it is not set, which means tolerate the taint forever (do not evict). Zero and negative values will be treated as 0 (evict immediately) by the system. If larger than zero, the time when the pod needs to be evicted is calculated as <time when taint was adedd> + <toleration seconds>.

value.description: value is the taint value the toleration matches to. If the operator is Exists, the value must be empty, otherwise just a regular string. Must be a label value.
